answer: A new key cannot be minted alone: an established identity must forge it and lock part of its own yield behind it. The lock releases at glacier pace, one slice per survived epoch, so the same stake cannot back a second head while held. If the sponsored identity is slashed, the sponsor's slice burns and its future capacity shrinks. Payout then scales with the health of the whole orchard that sponsor has grown. A farm of N clones needs N idle lockups plus N honest sponsors risking their own history, and history cannot be bought or pooled.
